title: Unique Sequence Reconstruction
hints: for the order to be unique, there must never be a real choice - what would it mean, in terms of the zero-in-degree queue in Kahn's algorithm, for there to be a choice at some step?
run Kahn's algorithm, but at every step check how many items currently have zero remaining in-degree

if that count is ever anything other than exactly 1 before you've placed all n items, the ordering is either ambiguous (more than one candidate) or impossible (a cycle, zero candidates) - return false immediately
if exactly one candidate is available at every single step, you've built the one and only valid order - compare it to org for equality
commonMistakes: checking only whether org itself respects every edge, without verifying that no OTHER valid ordering also exists
treating a cycle (zero available items at some step) the same as success instead of immediately returning false
stopping the uniqueness check early instead of verifying it holds at every single step of the algorithm

content.problemStatement:
You're given `n` items, labeled 0 to n - 1, and a list of ordering
constraints (`edges`), where each edge `[a, b]` means `a` must come
before `b` in any valid ordering. You're also given a candidate array
`org`, which is always a permutation of 0 to n - 1.

**Determine whether `org` is the one and only ordering of all n items that satisfies every constraint in `edges`, and return true if so, false otherwise.**

Return false whether because no valid ordering exists at all, because more than one valid ordering exists, or because org itself doesn't match the single valid ordering.
constraints: each edge [a, b] has 0 <= a, b < n
org is always a permutation of 0 to n - 1
notes: a cycle among the constraints, making no valid ordering possible at all
more than one item with zero remaining constraints at some step (an ambiguous ordering), even if org still 'looks' plausible
org is a valid ordering that respects every constraint, but it isn't the unique one
n = 1 with no edges - trivially unique
no edges at all with n > 1 - always ambiguous unless n is 1

sampleTestCases.explanation: the constraints force the exact order 0, 1, 2 with no other option at any step
item 2 has no constraint at all, so it could go anywhere - at the very first step, both 0 and 2 are available, which means the ordering is not unique
after placing 0, both 1 and 2 become available at the same time - either could legally come next, so the ordering is ambiguous
